headline: The writer
developers
hero.subtitle: Seven years turning APIs, SDKs, and developer platforms into documentation that ships adoption — and that AI agents now read to build on top.

about.quote: The gap between a good product and a successful product is often just documentation.
paragraphs: I'm Nabil Mohammed, Lead Technical Writer and the person developers thank when the docs actually made sense. I go by ==“Dev Docs Wizard”== because I believe that writing clear documentation is less about English and more about empathy for the developer experience.

Over 7+ years I've worked across Google Developer Groups, governmental research bodies, fintech startups, and one of the Middle East's largest e-commerce platforms. At Salla I manage documentation for 11 developer products, 440+ OpenAPI-compliant API endpoints and 96 tutorials, for a developer community of 75,000+ builders. My docs have driven a **75% improvement** in developer integrations.
When I'm not in the docs, I'm probably playing video games, rewatching Friends for the 12th time, or finding more elegant ways to explain complex things.

process.intro: Documentation treated as a core product, not an afterthought.

steps.title: Discover
steps.description: Embed with engineering and product. Read the code, attend standups, interview developers. Docs written from a distance show it.

steps.title: Architect
steps.description: Map the information architecture before writing a word. What does the developer need first? What will they search for at 2am?

steps.title: Write
steps.description: Precise, scannable, human. Every sentence earns its place. Written for the developer who is frustrated and needs to ship.

steps.title: Validate
steps.description: Real developers test the docs. If they get stuck, that is a documentation bug. Iterate until zero-to-working is frictionless.

steps.title: Measure
steps.description: Track support deflection, time-to-first-call, integration rates. Docs are a product and should have metrics.

aiWriting.intro: Documentation used to have one audience: developers. Not anymore. Today, AI agents, LLMs, and automated tools read docs to reason, generate code, and take action. I write for both.

pillars.title: 100% OpenAPI Compliant
pillars.body: Every Salla API endpoint I document is fully OpenAPI-compliant. Any LLM can import the spec and instantly understand auth, request shapes, response structures, and error codes. No human in the loop required. Structured docs are the interface.

pillars.title: Powering a Public MCP Server
pillars.body: I helped create the public Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for the Salla Partners Portal. When a developer asks Claude, Cursor, or any MCP-enabled agent to build on Salla, the agent reaches for this server. Around 95% of what it reads and acts on is content I wrote.
pillars.detail: ~95% content coverage · Claude · Cursor · VS Code

aiWriting.closing: The future of developer docs is not just human-readable. It is agent-ready, spec-compliant, and built to be consumed by whatever reads it.
